text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
- ADEVARUL
- Foreign investors can buy land in Romania, paper says in report on Tuesday's vote in the Senate, calling it the "first victory of the new parliamentary majority".
- Report on the appointment of Sorin Dimitriu as head of the State Ownership Fund.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Democratic Party MP Paula Ivanescu has asked for investigations into investment fund managed by SAFI, paper reports.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The United States' Bell and General Electric are looking for investments in Romania's aircraft industry.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Newspaper says that National Bank governor Mugur Isarescu will ask parliament today whether MPs can also hold senior positions in state banks.
ECONOMISTUL
- The budget deficit was financed through monetary issue, newspaper says.
- The competition law came into force on February 1 -- survey by Theodor Purcarea, state undersecretary at the Competition Council.
JURNALUL AFACERILOR
- Viorel Catarama will submit to parliament a draft law on stimulating and guaranteeing exports, the newspaper says.
- Romania might join the European Union by 2002-3, said Industry Minister Calin Popescu-Tariceanu.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Bucharest's Dimbovita river was polluted by large quantities of fuel oil, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Parliament commission supervising Romania's Intelligence Service (SRI) is expected to endorse bill allowing Romanians access to their files with the former Securitate secret police.
- Group of monarchists asked Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to restore ex-King Michael the Romanian citizenship which he was stripped of by the former Communists in 1947.
- Foreign Minister Adrian Severin proposed historic reconciliation between Russia and Romania, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The Romanian and Russian intelligence services signed a cooperation agreement in Moscow, the paper said.
- Some 1.5 tonnes of confiscated drugs are stored in the port of Constanta due to loopholes in the legislation on drugs.
- Leaders of big trade unions unhappy with social protection measures proposed by the government.
ADEVARUL
- Some 90 percent of Bucharest residents want Romania to gain early admission to NATO as the Alliance decides on its eastward expansion at a summit in July, an opinion poll shows.

- Miners in the Jiu Valley coalfield gathered some 500 million lei to pay a defence lawyer for their leader Miron Cosma, arrested over his role in the 1991 miner-led riots which ousted Romania's first post-communist government.
-- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264
